user.title: FoxESS - Modbus
user.description: How is your inverter connected to Home Assistant?

menu_options.tcp: Direct connection to the inverter's LAN port, or an RS485-to-Ethernet adapter using Modbus TCP
menu_options.rtu_over_tcp: RS485-to-Ethernet adapter using Modbus RTU over TCP
menu_options.serial: USB to RS485 adapter on a serial port

tcp.description: Enter the connection details for your inverter or adapter.

data_description.host: The hostname or IP address of the inverter (for a direct connection) or the adapter
data_description.port: The port of the inverter (502 for a direct connection) or the adapter
data_description.modbus_slave: This can be set from Settings -> Communication in the inverter menu
data_description.inverter_conn: Whether this is a direct connection to the inverter's LAN port, or an RS485-to-Ethernet adapter

data_description.poll_rate: How often the inverter is polled, in seconds
data_description.max_read: The maximum number of registers to read at a time. Increase this to speed up polling; look at the debug log for problems if you do!
data_description.round_sensor_values: Reduces Home Assistant database size by rounding and filtering sensor values

friendly_name.description: If you have more than one inverter, you can give this one a name to tell them apart. If you only have one inverter, you can leave this empty!

data_description.friendly_name: This is added to the end of all entity names, e.g. 'PV1 Power (Your Friendly Name)'
